response.rationale: C1 best combines the core diagnosis of fungal keratitis with raw-supported anatomic/distribution details: deep-stromal brown multilobular lesions and central pan-corneal plus peripheral deep-stromal infiltrates on OCT in a steroid-exposed post-DSAEK eye. R2 is the same core without this composite completeness; R1 is a distant immune-mechanism alternative without direct lesion support; R5 misuses corticosteroids as an independent cause; R4 is contradicted by explicit resolution of the prior caterpillar infection.

rejected.why: Correlated less-complete parent version; redundant with C1 and adds no independent raw evidence.
Corticosteroids are a predisposing risk factor, not an independent cause of brown multilobular deep corneal infiltrates.
Active Thaumetopoea pityocampa keratitis is disconfirmed by 'resolved prior to surgery' and lacks current lesion/OCT support.
